skills.name: Measure the density of regular and irregular solids

note.text:
Regular solid: measure its sides with a ruler (or vernier calipers), calculate the volume, find its mass on a balance, then ρ = m ÷ V.
Irregular solid: find its mass on a balance; find its volume by displacement (measuring cylinder or overflow can); then ρ = m ÷ V.
Sources of error: air bubbles on the stone, splashing, reading the meniscus from the side, water clinging to the stone if weighed after.
Weigh the solid before putting it in water.

sections.heading: Regular solids
sections.text:
For a block, cube or cylinder, find the volume by measuring and calculating, then weigh it.
A block {4} cm × {3} cm × {2} cm has V = {24} cm³. If its mass is {48} g, ρ = {48} ÷ {24} = {2} g/cm³.
Measure each side carefully: a small error in a length makes a bigger error in the volume.

sections.heading: Irregular solids
Good practice
sections.text:
• Weigh before wetting the stone.
• Lower it gently so water does not splash out.
• Shake off air bubbles: they add to the volume.
• Read the meniscus at eye level.
Repeat and take the mean to reduce errors.

key_words.meaning: a solid with a simple shape whose volume can be calculated
a solid with no simple shape
a can with a spout to collect the water an object displaces

examples: Stone {78} g raises water {50} → {60} mL: {7.8} g/cm³

mistake.wrong: Volume of the stone = final reading {60} mL
mistake.why: The water was already there; only the rise is due to the stone.

worked_example.problem: A stone has mass {m} g. Water in a measuring cylinder rises from {b} mL to {a} mL when the stone is put in. Find the density of the stone.
steps: ρ = m ÷ V = {m} ÷ {a - b} = {m / (a - b)} g/cm³.

cards.idea: Regular solid: volume from its measurements, mass from a balance.

check.prompt: A stone of mass {m} g is lowered into the cylinder shown. Find its density (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: Use the rise in level, not the final reading, as the volume.

solution: Volume = {2 * b + 2 * d} − {2 * b} = {2 * d} cm³.

cards.idea: Do the steps in a sensible order: weigh first, then put it in water.
example: A wet stone gives a wrong mass.

questions.prompt: A rectangular block is {l} cm × {w} cm × {h} cm and has mass {l * w * h * k / 10} g. Find its density (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: That is the mass. Divide it by the volume.
Use the volume (l × w × h), not the area of one face.

solution: ρ = {l * w * h * k / 10} ÷ {l * w * h} = {answer} g/cm³.

questions.prompt: A stone of mass {m} g is lowered into the cylinder shown. Find its density (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: Use the rise in level, not the final reading, as the volume.

solution: Volume = {2 * b + 2 * d} − {2 * b} = {2 * d} cm³.

questions.prompt: A brass key has a density of {r} g/cm³ and a mass of {r * V} g. What volume of water will it displace (cm³)?
Put the steps for finding the density of a stone in order.

items.text: Find the mass of the dry stone on a balance.
Pour water into a measuring cylinder and read the volume.
Lower the stone in gently on a thread and read the new volume.
Subtract the readings to get the volume of the stone.
Divide the mass by the volume.

questions.hint: Weigh the stone while it is still dry.

questions.prompt: A stone of mass {m} g is lowered into a full overflow can. The water that overflows has mass {v} g. Find the density of the stone (g/cm³).

misconceptions.explain: Density is the stone's mass divided by its volume.

solution: The overflow water has the same volume as the stone. Water has {1} g in each cm³, so V = {v} cm³.
